evidence.source: Shuowen Jiezi, Duan Yucai annotated online text
evidence.text: The entry says Shu people called a mother 姐 and 淮南 people called her 社; it describes 姐 as 女 plus phonetic 且 and gives a reading gloss. Duan's annotation adds that 社 and 姐 are close in sound and explains the entry as a regional word report. This is a Han-dictionary statement, not independent proof of the character's earliest graphic form or the word's full semantic history.
evidence.title: 說文解字第十二篇

evidence.source: Xiao Xu, Fudan Center for Research on Chinese Excavated Texts
evidence.field: discussion of 淮南謂母曰社
evidence.text: The article surveys interpretations and parallel forms for the regional mother term, including 姐/社 and forms such as 媞, 姼, 毑 and 她. It reports scholarly disagreement about whether these are phonetic records or related forms, and presents competing proposals; it does not establish a single derivational chain from mother to sister.
evidence.title: 蕭旭：《淮南子》古楚語舉證

evidence.field: Glyph origin; pronunciation; Old Chinese phonetic series
evidence.text: The page presents 姐 as 女 semantic plus 且 phonetic and lists Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese *ʔsjaːʔ for 姐 and *sʰjaːʔ, *ʔsa for 且. This is a secondary compilation of reconstructions, not direct evidence of ancient pronunciation. Its listed modern Mandarin for 姐 is jiě; use the cited official Unihan record for current metadata, with the caveat that the attempted Unicode record could not be opened in this research run.
evidence.title: 姐 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.source: Wiktionary, cited phonetic-series reconstruction attribution to Zhengzhang (2003)
evidence.text: In the Zhengzhang system as reported on this page, both 姐 and 且 have reconstructed forms with similar onset/rhyme material, though the page lists multiple readings for 且 and does not imply an exact one-to-one match in every reading. This supports reporting a proposed phonetic role as a historical analysis, not projecting modern jiě/qie pronunciation backward.

evidence.source: 蕭旭, Fudan Center article citing 《說文》 and 《方言》
evidence.field: discussion of historical senses and related kinship terms
evidence.text: The sources quoted in the article report regional mother-address usages, including Shu 姐 and 淮南 社, and cite 《方言》 for 南楚 usage of 母姼. The article's compilation indicates broader regional kinship vocabulary but does not date the first occurrence of the character 姐 or establish a semantic development from mother to older sister. A chronology for the modern elder-sister sense remains unverified here.
evidence.title: 蕭旭：《淮南子》古楚語舉證

evidence.source: 說文解字第十二篇 online text, entry 姊
evidence.text: The adjacent 姊 entry glosses the term as 女兄 and cites 《釋親》 and 《邶風》; this is evidence that the classical dictionary distinguishes 姊 as elder sister while the 姐 entry reports a regional word for mother. It does not on its own establish when 姐 acquired the elder-sister sense.

gaps: No visually inspected early glyph forms or secure excavated attestation for 姐 were found; the available inspected text describes a Shuowen small-seal entry but does not resolve earlier graphic development or possible corruption.

The Shuowen's regional sense is mother, whereas modern/common 姐 means elder sister/young woman. A dated chain linking these senses, earliest attestation for the elder-sister sense, and whether later use involves borrowing or semantic change remain unresolved.

The phonetic account 女 + 且 is explicitly in Shuowen and repeated in modern secondary sources. The original form/referent of 且 was not necessary to substantiate its later phonetic role here and was not independently established.

Exact Mandarin Unihan rows were unavailable in the required local datasets, and official Unicode record pages failed to open. Current readings need external verification from accessible official records.

The local Baxter–Sagart dataset contains 且 readings but no 姐 row found by exact search, preventing a direct within-system reconstruction comparison; Zhengzhang values must not be silently merged with Baxter–Sagart notation.

The search for earliest written examples and dated semantic stages did not establish dates beyond the Shuowen's Han compilation context; no chronology should be inferred from dictionary gloss ordering.
